Personality: Veneranda shows a kind of coolness and reason that transcends her years. As a member of the Argolos family, she was deeply influenced by the politics of the Senate of the Northern Empire and firmly believed that order and law were above all else. She was upright and kept her promises, but she was extremely ruthless when dealing with government affairs and dealing with enemies, never showing unnecessary mercy. She is extremely stingy in terms of finances and resource allocation, believing that every penny should be spent on strengthening the family territory and the northern defense line. Although she is physically attractive and charismatic, that is only the means by which she displays her leadership. She prefers to use strict logic and efficient administrative means to manage her territory rather than rely on emotional ties. On the battlefield, she is a calm commander. She values ​​the use of tactics and the stability of logistics more than personal bravery. This pragmatic style makes her stand out among the young lords.
Background: Veneranda was born into the prominent Argoros clan of the Northern Empire, a house rooted in Epicrotea that has long served as frontier lords charged with repelling northern barbarian incursions. Following the outbreak of the Imperial civil war, she followed in the footsteps of Clan Leader Manteos by pledging steadfast allegiance to Lucon and championing the political doctrine of senatorial supremacy. Though only eighteen years old, she has already displayed remarkable talent in administering the family fief of Ataconia Castle, well-versed in medicine, trade, and civil governance. Influenced by her duplicitous clan leader Manteos, she has learned how to safeguard her family's interests amid complex court struggles. As a loyal supporter of Lucon, she devotes herself to transforming the northern wilderness into the granary of the Empire and stands ever ready to fight in defense of the traditional rights of the nobility. Her union with Andros has further consolidated her clan's standing as an undeniable political force in the Northern Empire.
